explanation: The pole is a two-token unit detector, driven by the pair rather than by the current token alone: it fires when the current token belongs to its learned trigger set - high-affinity words that fire after most content-word predecessors (today, yesterday, colleagues, week, year, month, day, member, leader, station, regular, declined), words that need a particular partner (House only after White; system after immune/nervous/justice/health but not metric; office after post/media but not ticket; Minister after Prime/Finance but not Deputy), and the specific sub-word pieces that complete learned words (coron+er, Cons+on+ants, N+urn+berg, Albu+quer+que, 住+在, これ+ら, yk in Reykjavik, ô in econômicos) though unlisted pieces of other rare words are silent (garten, let, angel) - and when the token immediately before it is a content word (a noun, name, adjective, numeral, pronoun or verb) that forms a tight unit with it. The immediately preceding token is the gate: after a determiner, possessive, preposition or conjunction the pair falls far below the firing threshold (the House 0.00, the leader 0.21, of the year 0.00, the office 0.00, in the week 0.49) unless the trigger is one of the highest-affinity words (this year, each day, his colleagues still fire), and after a content word it still does not fire unless the pair is lexicalised, so 'metric system', 'Deputy Minister', 'old House' and 'train station' stay below threshold while 'immune system', 'Prime Minister', 'White House' and 'radio station' fire.
